- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1567-1582 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The bound is the earliest (min) created_at of any run on the head SHA in the branch's newest 30-run page. If head A was pushed, force-pushed to head B, and force-pushed back to head A, the branch page still holds A's first-push runs. The bound for A becomes its first push timestamp, and a completed PR-named review of B (created between the pushes) meets the timestamp filter on the PR-named-count path, consuming A's retry budget and skipping its editor-changes-lost recovery dispatch.
  WHY: The retry is skipped (return 0, no dispatch) for a head that has never had a recovery retry dispatched. This is fail-closed — no infinite loop, no lost data — and requires a force-push-back the PR's own pusher performs. The conformance audit flagged this as an HYPOTHESIS concern, documented in the progress log and plan Notes. The plan chose this bound explicitly (AD-1). Changing it to the latest run on the head or a per-push counter is a design tradeoff, not a demonstrated defect.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
